canada.lead: I went to Canada to study English and invest in my personal development.
canada.p1: English left the classroom and entered the routine. Talking, getting through the day, and figuring things out in another language turned fluency from an exercise into a real tool.
canada.p2: Living abroad was also personal development: autonomy, adaptation, and the decision to be somewhere new, away from the usual network. It stayed with me in how I communicate, choose, and hold a routine on my own.
canada.p3: The city and the distance from home widened my view. I carry that experience into international teams and products, on the same path as blockchain and fintechs.
